question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(3,0.3),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{x})(0.3)^{x}(0.7)^{3-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & =P(X\in \{2,3\}) \\  & =f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})(0.3)^{2}(0.7)^{3-2}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3})(0.3)^{3}(0.7)^{3-3} \\  & =3(0.3)^{2}(0.7)+1(0.3)^{3}(0.7)^{0} \\  & =0.216.\end{aligned}
$$
